matches.design:
Protocol: `--handoff <127.0.0.1:port>:<nonce>`. Old side `handoff(exe, args) -> Result<(), HandoffError>` in new crates/tze_hud_runtime/src/operator/handoff.rs: bind 127.0.0.1:0, spawn child with --handoff, wait <= 30 s for a `READY {version, sha, pid, nonce}` line with the matching nonce or child exit; on READY trigger shutdown (releasing ports and the single-instance mutex); on timeout/wrong nonce/early exit kill the child and stay up. New side `report_ready(spec)` fired from `WindowedConfig.on_first_present: Option<Box<dyn FnOnce() + Send>>` where frame_submitted first becomes true (windowed/mod.rs:~1800); full startup runs without service ports, then binds with bounded retry <= 10 s; mutex wait (<= 35 s) from the install bead. POST /admin/restart -> 202 then handoff(current_exe, original args captured in main and passed through WindowedConfig). Orchestration is generic over the child command so Linux tests use a fake child; timeouts are parameters.
Tests: child prints READY with right nonce -> Ok and shutdown triggered; wrong nonce, silence (timeout injected e.g. 200 ms) or early exit -> child killed, Err, old shutdown NOT triggered. Win-smoke: /admin/restart then poll /admin/status until pid changes and uptime_s resets within 60 s and the PSK still works.

matches.title: Clock domain types and validation
matches.description:
Sub-bead #1 of Epic 3 (Timing Model). Implement clock domain naming convention and type-safe timestamp wrappers.

Parent epic: rig-zyeo (Epic 3: Timing Model)
Dependencies: Epic 0 (rig-ge28, test infrastructure), Epic 1 (scene types for timestamp fields — not yet created)

## Spec requirements (v1-mandatory)

### Requirement: Clock Domain Naming Convention (spec lines 23-30)
All timestamp fields MUST encode their clock domain in the field name suffix: _wall_us for UTC wall clock (network clock domain) and _mono_us for monotonic system clock. Fields MUST NOT mix wall and mono in the same field. Fields without a clock-domain suffix are deltas or frame-relative values, not timestamps.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN a new timestamp field is added to any proto or Rust struct, THEN it MUST use _wall_us for UTC wall clock or _mono_us for monotonic clock; generic _us suffix without domain indicator MUST NOT be used for timestamps (spec line 29-30)

### Requirement: Clock Domain Separation (spec lines 10-21)
tze_hud MUST recognize four distinct clock domains: Display clock (vsync-driven), Monotonic system clock (OS monotonic, microsecond resolution), Network clock (agent-supplied UTC microseconds), and Media clock (GStreamer pipeline, post-v1 only). These domains MUST NOT be interchangeable.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN the compositor makes presentation timing decisions, THEN the display clock (vsync signal) MUST be the master reference (spec lines 15-17)
- WHEN the compositor measures stage latencies, deadline calculations, or lease TTL, THEN it MUST use the monotonic system clock (spec lines 19-21)

### Requirement: Timestamp Resolution and Format (spec lines 63-70)
All timestamps in the public API MUST use UTC microseconds since Unix epoch as uint64. Zero (0) MUST always mean "not set."

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN a timestamp field contains value 0, THEN the runtime MUST interpret it as "not set" (spec lines 68-70)

### Requirement: Injectable Clock (spec lines 313-324)
All timing paths MUST use an injectable clock source (Clock trait with now_us() and monotonic_us() methods). SystemClock (production) and SimulatedClock (tests, manually advanced) MUST be provided. The Clock trait MUST NOT have advance or set_time methods.

WHEN/THEN scenarios:
- WHEN a test uses SimulatedClock and advances time by 100ms, THEN all timing-dependent behavior MUST respond to the simulated time (spec lines 318-320)
- WHEN the Clock trait is used in production code, THEN it MUST only provide now_us() and monotonic_us(); no mutation methods (spec lines 322-324)

## Implementation

Recommended approach (goes beyond what spec literally requires but prevents the class of bugs the convention targets):
- WallUs newtype wrapper over u64 — enforces _wall_us domain at compile time
- MonoUs newtype wrapper over u64 — enforces _mono_us domain at compile time
- DurationUs for deltas (not a timestamp, no clock domain)
- Conversion between WallUs and MonoUs is explicit and requires a calibration offset
- Passing WallUs where MonoUs is expected MUST fail to compile

Existing code: crates/tze_hud_scene/src/clock.rs already has Clock trait, SystemClock, and TestClock. This bead extends that with domain types and validates the naming convention.

## Crate/file location
- Primary: crates/tze_hud_scene/src/clock.rs (extend existing Clock trait and types)
- New module: crates/tze_hud_scene/src/timing/domains.rs (WallUs, MonoUs, DurationUs newtypes)

## Relevant test scenes
- All 25 scenes use timestamps — this is foundational type infrastructure

## Cross-epic contracts
- Session-protocol (Epic 6) uses WallUs/MonoUs for session_open_wall_us, session_open_mono_us
- Input-model (Epic 5) uses MonoUs for interaction timestamps
- All scene types (Epic 1) must adopt _wall_us/_mono_us suffixes

## Acceptance criteria
- All timestamp fields in scene/protocol/session crates use correct _wall_us/_mono_us suffixes
- WallUs/MonoUs newtypes prevent cross-domain assignment at compile time
- Zero-value semantics (0 = "not set") encoded in type API
- Clock trait remains observation-only (no mutation methods in trait)
- SimulatedClock enables deterministic test timing

## v1-mandatory
- Clock Domain Separation, Clock Domain Naming Convention, Timestamp Resolution and Format, Injectable Clock

## v1-reserved exclusions
- None

## post-v1 exclusions
- Media clock domain (GStreamer pipeline clock, nanosecond resolution) — defined but not implemented
- ClockedMediaCue message class — proto enum value only

## Scope boundary (what this bead does NOT include)
- TimingHints struct (sub-bead #2)
- Presentation scheduling logic (sub-bead #2)
- Sync groups (sub-bead #3)
- Relative scheduling (sub-bead #4)

matches.title: Lease state machine — core states, transitions, and auditable events
matches.description:
Implement the core lease state machine per lease-governance/spec.md Requirement: Lease State Machine (lines 10-26) and Requirement: Lease Identity (lines 28-34).

## States
REQUESTED, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, ORPHANED, REVOKED, EXPIRED, DENIED, RELEASED

## Valid Transitions (spec line 11)
- REQUESTED->ACTIVE (granted)
- REQUESTED->DENIED (denied)
- ACTIVE->SUSPENDED (safe mode)
- ACTIVE->ORPHANED (disconnect)
- ACTIVE->EXPIRED (TTL elapsed)
- ACTIVE->REVOKED (viewer dismiss, budget policy)
- ACTIVE->RELEASED (agent releases)
- SUSPENDED->ACTIVE (safe mode exit)
- SUSPENDED->REVOKED (max suspension time exceeded)
- ORPHANED->ACTIVE (reconnect within grace)
- ORPHANED->EXPIRED (grace period elapsed)
Terminal states: DENIED, REVOKED, EXPIRED, RELEASED — no further transitions possible.

## Lease Identity (spec lines 28-34, Requirement: Lease Identity)
Each lease carries: LeaseId (UUIDv7, time-ordered, SceneId type), namespace (agent identity string), session_id (parent session), granted_at_wall_us (UTC microseconds), ttl_ms (0 = indefinite), renewal_policy, capability_scope, resource_budget, lease_priority.

## Operations Requiring a Lease (spec lines 37-46, Requirement: Operations Requiring a Lease)
CreateTile, InsertNode, ReplaceNode, RemoveNode, UpdateTileBounds, UpdateTileExpiry MUST require an ACTIVE lease. Guest MCP ZonePublish MUST NOT require a lease. CreateTab, RemoveTab, read operations MUST NOT require a lease.

## Wire Protocol Integration (spec lines 307-314, Requirement: Wire Protocol Integration)
Lease messages flow over primary session stream within SessionMessage envelope:
- LeaseRequest (client->server): field 21
- LeaseResponse (server->client): field 31
- LeaseSuspend: field 47, LeaseResume: field 48, LeaseStateChange: field 49

## Lease Caps (spec lines 298-305, Requirement: Lease Caps)
Max 64 leases per runtime (all agents), max 8 default (64 hard max) per session, max 64 tiles per lease, max 64 nodes per tile.

## Each transition produces an auditable event.

## WHEN/THEN Scenarios from Spec

Scenario: Lease granted (spec lines 15-17)
- WHEN an agent sends a LeaseRequest with valid capabilities and budget within limits
- THEN the lease transitions from REQUESTED to ACTIVE and the agent receives LeaseResponse with result = GRANTED

Scenario: Lease denied (spec lines 19-21)
- WHEN an agent sends a LeaseRequest requesting capabilities beyond its session grants
- THEN the lease transitions to DENIED and the agent receives LeaseResponse with result = DENIED and populated deny_reason

Scenario: Invalid transition rejected (spec lines 23-25)
- WHEN a lease is in EXPIRED state
- THEN no further transitions are possible (terminal state)

Scenario: Lease identity fields populated (spec lines 32-34)
- WHEN a lease is granted
- THEN the LeaseResponse includes a UUIDv7 LeaseId, the granted TTL, priority, budget, and expiry timestamp

Scenario: Tile mutation without active lease (spec lines 41-43)
- WHEN an agent attempts InsertNode but its lease is in SUSPENDED state
- THEN the mutation is rejected with SAFE_MODE_ACTIVE error

Scenario: Guest zone publish without lease (spec lines 45-46)
- WHEN a guest agent publishes to a zone via MCP ZonePublishToken
- THEN the publish succeeds without requiring a lease

Scenario: Runtime-wide lease limit (spec lines 303-305)
- WHEN 64 leases are active across all agents and a new lease is requested
- THEN the request is denied with MAX_RUNTIME_LEASES_EXCEEDED

Scenario: Lease messages on session stream (spec lines 312-314)
- WHEN an agent sends a LeaseRequest
- THEN it is carried as field 21 of the SessionMessage oneof on the existing session stream

Scenario: Sub-millisecond lease grant (spec lines 248-251, Requirement: Lease Grant Latency)
- WHEN an agent sends a valid LeaseRequest
- THEN the LeaseResponse with result = GRANTED is emitted within 1ms

## State Machine Diagram Reference
See lease-governance/spec.md lines 10-11 for the complete valid transitions table.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All LeaseStateMachine trait contract tests from Epic 0 (rig-ho4b) pass
- Every valid transition verified
- Every invalid transition rejected with structured error
- lease_expiry test scene passes
- Lease identity fields correctly populated on grant
- Operations requiring a lease correctly gated
- Lease caps enforced

## Crate/File Location
Extract from crates/tze_hud_scene/src/graph.rs into dedicated crates/tze_hud_scene/src/lease/mod.rs (state machine core), crates/tze_hud_scene/src/lease/types.rs (LeaseId, LeaseState enum, LeaseIdentity struct).

- Requirement: Lease Grant Latency (spec lines 244-251)
- Requirement: Lease Caps (spec lines 298-305)
- Requirement: Wire Protocol Integration (spec lines 307-314)

## v1-reserved exclusions
- Budget Renegotiation (spec lines 317-319)
- Grace Period Acceleration (spec lines 334-341)

## post-v1 exclusions

## What This Does NOT Include

- Disconnect grace or orphan handling (bead #3)

matches.title: Trait contract test harnesses for 5 v1 subsystems
matches.description:
Define Rust traits encoding spec requirements for 5 core subsystems, with companion test suites written against the trait. Any correct implementation must satisfy the tests. Tests compile but fail (or are #[ignore]d) until implementation lands.

## Spec Links

- lease-governance/spec.md lines 10-25: state machine (REQUESTED→ACTIVE→SUSPENDED/ORPHANED/EXPIRED/REVOKED/RELEASED/DENIED)
- lease-governance/spec.md lines 71-90: auto-renewal semantics (MANUAL, AUTO_RENEW at 75% TTL, ONE_SHOT)
- lease-governance/spec.md lines 92-104: safe mode (ACTIVE→SUSPENDED, TTL paused, resume ≤2 frames)
- lease-governance/spec.md lines 114-122: max suspension time (300,000ms default, revoke oldest-first)
- lease-governance/spec.md lines 132-155: orphan grace period (30,000ms, detection via heartbeat timeout 3×5000ms=15,000ms)
- lease-governance/spec.md lines 169-185: budget soft/hard limits (80%/100%)
- lease-governance/spec.md lines 187-200: three-tier budget enforcement ladder (Warning at 80%, Throttle at 85-95%, Revocation at 100% hard limit)
- policy-arbitration/spec.md lines 10-17: seven-level stack (Human Override → Safety → Privacy → Security → Attention → Resource → Content)
- policy-arbitration/spec.md lines 91-104: Level 2 Privacy Evaluation (VisibilityClassification vs ViewerClass redaction matrix)
- policy-arbitration/spec.md lines 143-166: attention budget (20/min per-agent, 10/min per-zone)
- policy-arbitration/spec.md lines 194-199: per-frame evaluation order and <200µs budget
- scene-events/spec.md lines 5-16: three-category taxonomy (Input, Scene, System)
- scene-events/spec.md lines 35-46: event type naming convention (scene.<object>.<action>)
- scene-events/spec.md lines 50-65: interruption classes (CRITICAL > HIGH > NORMAL > LOW > SILENT)
- scene-events/spec.md lines 92-103: quiet hours queue (FIFO per-zone, LatestWins coalesce, max 100)
- scene-events/spec.md lines 107-122: agent event emission (capability check, 4KB limit, 10 events/sec rate limit)
- scene-events/spec.md lines 156-183: subscription categories and capability mapping
- resource-store/spec.md lines 5-16: BLAKE3 content-addressed identity
- resource-store/spec.md lines 20-27: resource immutability
- resource-store/spec.md lines 31-42: v1 types (IMAGE_RGBA8, IMAGE_PNG, IMAGE_JPEG, FONT_TTF, FONT_OTF)
- resource-store/spec.md lines 57-68: chunked upload protocol
- resource-store/spec.md lines 72-79: small resource fast path (≤64KB inline)
- resource-store/spec.md lines 102-113: deduplication (hash hit → <100µs)
- resource-store/spec.md lines 117-124: concurrent upload limit (≤4 in-flight)
- resource-store/spec.md lines 128-147: reference counting semantics
- configuration/spec.md lines 10-21: TOML format, parse error line/column
- configuration/spec.md lines 23-34: file resolution chain (CLI → env → cwd → XDG)
- configuration/spec.md lines 36-47: minimal config requirements
- configuration/spec.md lines 49-82: built-in profiles (full-display, headless, mobile rejection)
- configuration/spec.md lines 84-99: profile auto-detection
- configuration/spec.md lines 101-112: budget escalation prevention
- configuration/spec.md lines 149-150: capability vocabulary (canonical wire-format names)

## Traits to Define

### 1. LeaseStateMachine
Encode lease lifecycle from lease-governance/spec.md:
- States: REQUESTED, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, ORPHANED, EXPIRED, REVOKED, RELEASED, DENIED
- Methods: request(), activate(), suspend(), resume(), orphan(), expire(), revoke(), release(), deny()
- Queries: state(), ttl_remaining(), is_terminal(), can_transition_to()
- Clock injection via TestClock for TTL/grace period testing
- Budget enforcement thresholds: Warning at 80%, Throttle at 85-95%, Revocation at 100% hard limit (lease-governance/spec.md lines 187-200)

### 2. PolicyEvaluator
Encode policy-arbitration/spec.md:
- Input: typed PolicyContext (safety state, privacy classifications, capabilities, attention counters, resource budgets, zone contention)
- Output: PolicyDecision with applied_level, action, reason
- Must evaluate levels in order (0→6), short-circuit on first decisive result
- Level 2 (Privacy): VisibilityClassification vs ViewerClass redaction matrix (policy-arbitration/spec.md lines 91-104)
- Budget check: total evaluation <200µs (policy-arbitration/spec.md lines 194-199)
- Attention budget tracking: per-agent 20/min, per-zone 10/min

### 3. EventRouter
Encode scene-events/spec.md:
- Methods: emit(), subscribe(), unsubscribe(), enter_quiet_hours(), exit_quiet_hours()
- Event type validation: naming convention enforcement (scene.<object>.<action>)
- Interruption classification: route by class, enforce quiet hours rules
- Subscription filtering: category→capability mapping per lines 156-183
- Rate limiting: 10 events/sec per agent, 4KB payload limit

### 4. ResourceStore
Encode resource-store/spec.md:
- Methods: upload_start(), upload_chunk(), upload_complete(), upload_inline(), get(), delete(), gc()
- Content addressing: BLAKE3 hash identity
- Deduplication: hash hit returns existing, was_deduplicated=true
- Type validation: reject non-v1 types
- Concurrent limit: ≤4 in-flight uploads
- Reference counting: increment on node creation, decrement on deletion

### 5. ConfigLoader
Encode configuration/spec.md:
- Methods: parse(), normalize(), validate(), freeze()
- File resolution: ordered chain with first-found semantics
- Profile resolution: full-display, headless, mobile (rejected), auto-detection
- Budget escalation prevention: custom cannot exceed base values
- Capability vocabulary validation: reject unknown capability names
- Includes rejection: v1 does not support config includes

## WHEN/THEN Scenarios (representative subset)

LeaseStateMachine:
- WHEN lease is REQUESTED and activate() called THEN state becomes ACTIVE
- WHEN lease is ACTIVE and TTL elapses THEN state becomes EXPIRED
- WHEN lease is ACTIVE and safe mode entered THEN state becomes SUSPENDED, TTL paused
- WHEN lease is SUSPENDED and safe mode exits THEN state becomes ACTIVE within 2 frames (33.2ms), TTL resumes with adjusted expiry
- WHEN lease is SUSPENDED for >300,000ms THEN state becomes REVOKED (oldest-first)
- WHEN lease is ORPHANED and agent reconnects within 30,000ms THEN state becomes ACTIVE
- WHEN lease is ORPHANED and grace period elapses THEN state becomes EXPIRED
- WHEN lease is EXPIRED/REVOKED/RELEASED/DENIED and any transition attempted THEN error (terminal states)
- WHEN ONE_SHOT lease is SUSPENDED THEN TTL paused; on resume, adjusted expiry = original_expiry + suspension_duration
- WHEN budget at 80% THEN BudgetWarning emitted, mutations still accepted (Warning tier)
- WHEN budget at 85-95% THEN mutation rate throttled (Throttle tier)
- WHEN budget at 100% THEN MutationBatch rejected atomically with BUDGET_EXCEEDED (Revocation tier)

PolicyEvaluator:
- WHEN safety event (GPU failure) fires THEN Level 1 short-circuits, lower levels skipped
- WHEN privacy redaction required THEN Level 2 applied before security/attention/resource checks (policy-arbitration/spec.md lines 91-104)
- WHEN capability check fails THEN Level 3 returns CAPABILITY_REQUIRED within <5µs
- WHEN attention budget at 80% THEN AttentionBudgetWarningEvent emitted
- WHEN attention budget at 100% THEN mutations coalesced (latest-wins within agent+zone)
- WHEN total evaluation exceeds 200µs THEN budget violation logged

EventRouter:
- WHEN event emitted during quiet hours with class=NORMAL THEN queued in FIFO
- WHEN event emitted during quiet hours with class=LOW THEN discarded
- WHEN event emitted during quiet hours with class=CRITICAL THEN delivered immediately
- WHEN quiet hours exit THEN queued events delivered in FIFO order
- WHEN LatestWins zone in quiet hours receives 2 publishes THEN only latest kept in queue
- WHEN agent emits event without required capability THEN rejected
- WHEN agent exceeds 10 events/sec THEN rate limited

ResourceStore:
- WHEN identical bytes uploaded twice THEN same ResourceId returned, was_deduplicated=true, latency <100µs
- WHEN non-v1 type uploaded THEN rejected with TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED
- WHEN 5th concurrent upload attempted THEN rejected with RESOURCE_TOO_MANY_UPLOADS
- WHEN chunked upload completes with hash mismatch THEN rejected
- WHEN resource refcount reaches 0 THEN eligible for GC

ConfigLoader:
- WHEN TOML has syntax error THEN parse error includes line and column
- WHEN profile=mobile THEN rejected with CONFIG_MOBILE_PROFILE_NOT_EXERCISED
- WHEN custom profile exceeds base budget THEN rejected with BUDGET_ESCALATION
- WHEN unknown capability in agent config THEN rejected with UNKNOWN_CAPABILITY
- WHEN config includes used THEN rejected (v1 does not support includes)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] 5 Rust traits defined in dedicated modules
- [ ] Each trait has ≥10 #[test] functions encoding spec WHEN/THEN scenarios
- [ ] Tests use TestClock for all time-dependent assertions
- [ ] Tests compile against the trait (not a concrete type) — use generic test functions
- [ ] Tests fail or are #[ignore]d until correct implementation provided
- [ ] Total: ≥50 test functions across all 5 trait modules
- [ ] No implementation code — traits define the contract only

## Crate/File Locations

- LeaseStateMachine: crates/tze_hud_scene/src/lease/mod.rs (new module) + tests in crates/tze_hud_scene/src/lease/tests.rs
- PolicyEvaluator: crates/tze_hud_scene/src/policy/mod.rs + tests
- EventRouter: crates/tze_hud_scene/src/events/mod.rs + tests (or crates/tze_hud_protocol/src/events/)
- ResourceStore: crates/tze_hud_scene/src/resource/mod.rs + tests
- ConfigLoader: crates/tze_hud_scene/src/config/mod.rs + tests (or new crate crates/tze_hud_config/)

## What This Does NOT Include

This bead produces TRAIT DEFINITIONS AND TEST HARNESSES only. It does NOT:
- Implement the traits (that is implementation work for later beads)
- Add wire protocol tests (that is bead #4)
- Add pixel/rendering tests (that is bead #5)
- Modify existing runtime or compositor code
